title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: the 1986 'Analysis situs' notes build an axiomatic theory of 'ateliers' (workshops). An atelier is a set of abstract 'figures' with an order ≤ (subfigure) and a second relation ≪, subject to axioms At1–At8. Fig(L) is the concrete atelier of figures (subsets) of a set L of points or 'multilocalités'. The page finishes an argument from p.51 and then defines when an atelier is 'set-theoretic'.

(1) End of the argument. On p.51 a morphism f: F' → F of ateliers is called a plongement (embedding) if its image is a sub-atelier and f induces an isomorphism onto that image. Explicitly, this means two conditions:
- a') for every F', the map Sousfig(F') → Sousfig(f(F')), G' ↦ f(G'), is bijective (in particular surjective onto the subfigures of f(F'));
- b') f(G') ≤ f(F') ⇒ G' ≤ F' (f reflects the order).
The page says these conditions are clearly necessary. For sufficiency it suffices to check that f is injective and that the conditions imply b'). The proof: if f(G') ≤ f(F'), surjectivity in a') gives some Ḡ' ≤ F' with f(Ḡ') = f(G'). Injectivity of f then forces G' = Ḡ', so G' ≤ F'. In modern terms: an injective monotone map that is surjective on each down-set onto the down-set of the image is an order embedding onto a down-closed image.

(2) Definition. An atelier F satisfying At1–At8 is called 'ensembliste' (set-theoretic) if the canonical map F → Fig(L) is a plongement. Grothendieck also allows that there might be a stricter variant of the notion. By (1.53) on p.46 this is equivalent to the axiom At ens 1: for all F, G in F, multloc(F) ≪ multloc(G) ⇒ F ≪ G. In words, the relation between figures is detected by their underlying sets of 'multilocalités' (points). This is a 'spatiality' or representability condition: the abstract poset of figures embeds faithfully into a power-set-type atelier.

(3) Remarks.
- It suffices to impose At ens 1 when F and G are themselves multilocalities. It would be 'plus joli' (nicer) to state the axiom with x, y ∈ M directly.
- The embedding F ↪ Fig(L) is not required to be 'gracieux'. An example follows: E a tame ('modéré') topological space and M one of its simplicial multilocality structures (topological or tame).
- The next page explains the point of this example. Compatibility of simplices (the intersection must be a single convex simplex) is finer than compatibility of the associated polyhedral figures. It closes with the question of which sub-ateliers of Fig(L) arise in this way.

The page serves Grothendieck's programme of an axiomatic 'tame topology' (topologie modérée) of polyhedral or stratified figures, here the problem of when abstract figure-structures are concretely realized by sets of points.
errors: The proof labels are muddled. The step 'there exists Ḡ' ≤ F' with f(Ḡ') = f(G')' uses the surjectivity part of a'), not b'). The step G' = Ḡ' uses injectivity of f, not 'a)'. The mathematics is correct once the labels are fixed.

The claimed equivalence of 'plongement' with At ens 1 relies on (1.53) p.46, which is not visible here. It also presumably needs the map to be injective and down-set-surjective, which At1–At8 must guarantee. Unverifiable from this page.

ideas.what: Characterization of embeddings of ateliers: injective + down-set bijectivity implies order reflection
ideas.modern_name: order embedding onto a down-closed subposet / full sub-structure embedding

ideas.what: 'Ensembliste' ateliers: abstract figure-structures whose canonical map to the power-set atelier Fig(L) of points is an embedding; axiom At ens 1
ideas.modern_name: spatiality / representability condition (analogous to spatial locales, Stone-type representation of a poset of figures by point sets)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Stone (1936) for lattice representation; spatial locales: Ehresmann/Isbell/Johnstone tradition
ideas.where_published: Tame topology programme only sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); ateliers formalism unpublished

ideas.what: Example: simplicial structures on a tame space, where compatibility of simplices is finer than compatibility of the associated polyhedral figures
ideas.usually_credited_to: PL topology; o-minimal triangulation theorem (van den Dries)

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates (with the next page) the problem of characterizing which sub-ateliers of Fig(L) arise from abstract ateliers. This amounts to a representation theorem for his axiomatic tame-topology structures, and it appears to be left open.
missed.quote: On dit que l'atelier F est ensembliste ... si l'application canonique F → Fig(L) est un plongement
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a point-set representation question for axiomatic tame geometry, comparable to spatiality of locales or to the passage from o-minimal structures to their definable-set lattices. It is of modest interest unless the full ateliers formalism is reconstructed.

deep.surprise_reason: A technical definitional page in an unpublished axiomatic framework (ateliers) for tame topology. The lemma is routine order theory and the 'ensembliste' condition is a natural spatiality axiom; the framework itself is little known, but this page holds no striking result.
transcription_corrections: In the Dém the step yielding Ḡ' logically uses a') (surjectivity), and the step G' = Ḡ' uses injectivity of f. The transcription's 'Par b')' and 'par a)' should be checked against the image.
At ens 1 reads: ∀F,G∈F, multloc(F) ≪ multloc(G) ⇒ F ≪ G (the 'multloc(F)' sits on the line below in the manuscript).
Left margin reads roughly 'Pour une variante[?] cf VI p.12' (written vertically, with 'VI' boxed).
Line 1: 'C'est évidemment nécessaire. Pour que ça suffise'.
The 'satisfaisant At 1 – At 8' insertion belongs after 'l'atelier F'.
